significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that conditional subliminal traits comprise "two dissociable early-layer directions" and that payload dormancy predictively couples lower activation during repair to greater persistence; this is a form-(iii) relation between measurable payload activity and erasure, backed by a form-(ii) causal decomposition rather than merely an existence claim. It would establish both the stealth-and-stickiness phenomenon and a mechanism that fixes further expectations: detector activation should invoke the payload without the trigger, payload removal should preserve detection, and repair success should vary with payload activation; this bears directly on the persistence questions raised by Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning and Hubinger et al.'s Sleeper Agents. Verified false is also determinate and informative: it would rule out the separable detector/payload and dormancy-based durability accounts, while failure of the stickiness asymmetry would show that gating supplies concealment but not added repair resistance. Topic substitution check: replacing these specific factorization and activity-erasure claims with merely "extend subliminal learning" would not support this score, because the two-part causal account and predictive coupling are materially stronger than the topic's obvious direction-or-transfer hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are "activation-level, trigger-search audits (probing for a latent payload direction that is silent behaviorally)" and the "Conditional Subliminal Trait diagnostic suite." The audit is ex ante because it is intended to detect a dormant payload before behavior-only repair certification or model deployment, giving auditors an action window rather than merely explaining an observed failure. Although directions would require per-model re-extraction, the asserted conclusion predicts what should survive recalibration—cross-trigger reuse of the "SAME payload direction" and an activity-versus-erasure relationship—while the downstream users include safety auditors and backdoor-defense practitioners; reach is nevertheless short of universal because cross-model invariance is not asserted and the claim acknowledges possible trigger-, trait-, and family-specificity. Topic substitution check: the generic subliminal-learning topic supplies neither this pre-deployment audit nor the transferable detector/payload relation, so the score rests on claim-specific handles rather than topic importance.
